label: Tail
tip: The pitch the kick settles on. Tune it to the root note of your track so kick and sub bass add up instead of fighting. A1 is 55 Hz, F#1 is 46.25 Hz.

label: Start
tip: Pitch at the very first moment. A high start (about 800 to 1000 Hz) gives the snap.

label: Sweep
tip: How fast the pitch falls from Start to Tail. About 25 to 35 ms is tight. Around 80 ms starts to sound like a laser.

label: Curve
tip: Shape of the fall. 1.00 is exponential. Lower drops faster at the start, higher drops slower at the start.

label: Level
tip: Loudness of the click, the short high knock that lets you hear the kick inside a wall of supersaws.

label: Freq
tip: Centre frequency of the click. Roughly 2 to 5 kHz cuts through leads.

label: Length
tip: How long the click lasts. Longer clicks sound harder and more clicky.

label: Body
tip: Extra punch in the first tens of milliseconds, while the pitch is still falling through the chest range.

label: Sub
tip: Level of the tail that sits on the Tail pitch. This is the low weight you feel.

label: Hold
tip: Keeps the kick at full level for a few ms before it decays, so the top of the hit lands harder.

label: Decay
tip: Time from the end of Hold until the kick is silent (-60 dB). The marker on the waveform shows one 16th note at your tempo.

label: Swell
tip: Lets the low body of the kick grow over the first milliseconds instead of starting at full level. Real trance kicks start with a quiet, fast pitch drop and the click on top, then the body swells in. 40 ms is typical. 0 is off.

label: Shape
tip: Shape of the decay. 1.0 fades steadily from the start. Higher keeps the kick near full level for most of its length, then drops fast at the end. Real trance kicks sit around 4 to 5.

label: Drive
tip: Smooth symmetric saturation. Adds harmonics so the kick is heard on small speakers. Level is matched, so it does not just get louder.

label: Transistor
tip: Asymmetric saturation with even harmonics and extra low weight.

label: Fuzz
tip: Smooth fuzz stage. Keep low for clean kicks, push for hard dance.

label: Clip
tip: Soft clipper at the end. More clip makes the kick denser and louder without going over 0 dB.

label: Amount
tip: Master amount of the Sauce chain. 0 is off. Raise it to blend in all the stages at once, then shape them with the knobs next to it.

label: Punch
tip: Saturates the 120 to 800 Hz band in parallel. That is where a kick is felt in the chest on small and large speakers. More punch, more body.

label: Thump
tip: Saturates the sub below 120 Hz so the low note grows harmonics at 2 and 3 times its pitch. Gives weight you can hear on laptop speakers, and a little more low level.

label: Bloom
tip: A soft swell in the low tail at about 40 to 80 ms. Makes the kick breathe and pump, so the tail lifts after the hit instead of just dying away.

label: Crack
tip: Lifts and rounds the top band above 800 Hz, strongest in the first 10 ms. Sharper attack that cuts through a full mix.

label: Mix
tip: How much of the glue compressor is blended in. 0 is off. Shape it with Threshold, Ratio, Attack and Release. Works even when Sauce Amount is 0. Fills the gaps in the tail so the kick feels thick and solid.

label: Loud
tip: Makes the kick denser and louder while the peak stays the same: up to 6 dB more average level, with the peaks shaved smoothly instead of hard clipped.

label: Thresh
tip: Where the glue compressor starts working, in dB below the kick peak. Lower means more of the kick gets squeezed.

label: Ratio
tip: How hard it squeezes above the threshold. 2 is gentle, 6 is firm, 20 is almost a limiter.

label: Attack
tip: How slowly the compressor grabs. Longer lets more of the click and punch through first. Try 30 to 50 ms for a hard punch.

label: Release
tip: How fast it lets go. Short brings the tail up between beats, long keeps it smooth.

label: Limiter
tip: Limiter on or off.

label: Push
tip: How hard the limiter is pushed. It raises the kick, then stops the peaks from growing, so the body gets louder and punchier.

label: Mud
tip: Cuts the boxy zone around 250 Hz, up to 12 dB. That is where kicks sound cardboard or cheap.

label: Chest
tip: Wide boost around 80 Hz, up to 8 dB. The part you feel in your chest.

label: Shine
tip: Boosts everything above 2.5 kHz, up to 15 dB. Brings out the click so the kick cuts through.

label: Ceiling
tip: True-peak ceiling in dB. If the kick would go above this after conversion (inter-sample peaks), it is turned down to sit exactly on it. -0.3 dB is safe for any export.

label: Align
tip: Phase align. Flips a layer upside down if it starts against the body, so click, attack and body push the same way and the punch is the same every time.

label: Output
tip: Output level in dB. Watch the meter on the right.

label: Level
tip: Loudness of layer A.

label: Pitch
tip: Pitch of layer A in semitones. Built-in sounds move their tone or filter. Your own sound plays faster or slower.

label: Start
tip: Trims the first ms off a sound, to cut silence or a soft attack. Fine range 0 to 40 ms; hold Shift while dragging for even finer steps.

label: Len
tip: How long the layer lasts. For built-in sounds it is the decay time. For your own sound it is the part that plays, with a short fade at the end.

label: Delay
tip: Starts the layer this many ms after the kick. Use it to line the top up with the body of the kick.

label: HP
tip: High-pass filter. Cuts the lows of the layer so it does not fight the sub. At 20 Hz it is off.

label: LP
tip: Low-pass filter. Softens the highs of the layer. At 20 kHz it is off.

tip: Loudness of layer B.
